Hi Jordan — great speaking with you today. Thanks for walking me through Acme's evaluation priorities. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before the engineering kickoff: 

Call recap / goals
- Primary goal: validate Redwood's inference latency and cost profiles on Acme's summarization workload (avg. 512 tokens, 95th pct latency target < 350ms)
- Success criteria: 95th percentile latency < 350ms for typical test traffic, cost per 1M tokens within 20% of our projection, model output pass-rate on your sample eval set >= 92%
- Data constraints: no PHI, PII masked; all logs access-controlled

POC environment options (we discussed):
1) Hosted trial (fastest) — Redwood-hosted endpoint, shared infra, quick to spin up (1–3 business days). Good for initial functional evaluation and latency baselining.
2) Dedicated sandbox — reserved GPU pool for Acme (predictable throughput, better isolation). Takes ~1 week to provision with a reserved config.
3) VPC trial (private) — Your team owns the network/VPC peering, private control plane. Best for security/regulatory checks. Provisioning depends on networking windows (1–2 weeks).

Recommended evaluation plan
- Phase 1 (Week 0–1): Hosted baseline — Redwood provides a hosted sandbox and sample scripts so Acme can run the eval set. Deliverables: baseline latency/cost report, initial qualitative feedback.
- Phase 2 (Week 2): If isolation or throughput questions arise, move to Dedicated sandbox for sustained load testing. Deliverables: throughput report, model tuning notes.
- Phase 3 (Week 3–4): If required by security/compliance, move to VPC trial for final validation. Deliverables: security checklist + audit evidence.

Ownership & next steps
- Redwood: Marissa (sales lead) — commercial MLP and timeline; Michael (solutions engineer) — technical onboarding and test harness; Neha (CS engineer) — config, warmup scripts, and monitoring dashboards.
- Acme: Jordan (engineering lead) — owns running evals and sharing results; Infra Team — network/VPC coordination if we go private.

Action items (can we confirm by Tue?):
1) Jordan: agree to start with Hosted baseline?
2) Jordan: share the sample eval set (or a subset) and expected QPS for the test window.
3) Marissa/Redwood: provide POC checklist + kickoff availability slots (Michael and Neha available Wed/Thu next week).

Attachments: I attached the Redwood POC checklist with required access and typical timelines.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

Best,
Marissa

Short answers up front:
- Hosted sandbox: request/response bodies are not persisted to long-term logs by default. We keep ephemeral logs for 72 hours for debugging; this can be reduced or disabled for the POC.
- Dedicated sandbox: provides instance-level isolation and longer retention options if your compliance team needs that.
- VPC: full private connectivity; Redwood will still need outbound access to our control plane endpoints for metrics unless you request an air-gapped deployment.
